data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name Ignatius, Ignace signifies 'little fire' or 'little flame'. This name is believed to have been given to early Christians who were lit with the fire of the Holy Spirit during baptism. The name Ignace carries the meaning “Latin: 'Fiery, Passionate'” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ignace usually hope their child will grow to embody latin: 'fiery, passionate' and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Ιγνάτιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιγνάτιος προέρχεται από το λατινικό Ignatius, που σημαίνει 'γεννημένος από τη φωτιά' ή 'φωτιά'. Στην πνευματική διάσταση, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει την αναγέννηση και την πνευματική φωτιά που οδηγεί στην αλλαγή και την ανάπτυξη. Στην Εκκλησία των πρώτων χρόνων, το όνομα Ιγνάτιος συνδέθηκε με τον Άγιο Ιγνάτιο, επίσκοπο Αντιοχείας.

in_latin.name: Ignatius
in_latin.meaning: Born of fire or fiery one
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ignatius is derived from the Latin word 'ignis,' meaning fire. It signifies one born of fire or a fiery individual. In early Christian tradition, Ignatius was a name associated with spiritual fervor and zeal. Saint Ignatius of Antioch, an early Christian bishop and martyr, contributed to the name's religious significance.

in_english.name: Ignace
in_english.meaning: Fiery one or born of fire
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ignace, derived from Latin 'Ignatius,' means 'fiery one' or 'born of fire.' Etymologically, it connects to the Latin 'ignis,' meaning fire. Ignace symbolizes spiritual fire, renewal, and fervor. Historically, Saint Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, and Saint Ignatius of Antioch, an early Christian bishop, contributed to the name's spiritual significance. The name represents passion, zeal, and spiritual dedication.
